title: Quaintly Flaky Middle Eastern Kabocha Tagine
description: A nostalgic Middle Eastern dish featuring kabocha, with a flaky texture and a hint of mustard, made with mortar-pestle-pound technique, shojin-friendly. It is a hearty and comforting meal.
instructions: In a large mortar, pound the onion and garlic until well combined.
Add the cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper to the mortar and pound until well combined.
In a large bowl, toss the kabocha squash with the mortar mixture until the squash is well coated.
Roll out the pastry dough to a large rectangle, about 1/4 inch thick.
Spread the dijon mustard evenly over the center of the dough, leaving a 1 inch border around the edges.
Arrange the kabocha squash mixture over the mustard, leaving a 1 inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the pastry up over the filling, pressing gently to seal.
Brush the pastry with olive oil and cut a few slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
Bake the tagine for 40 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and the squash is tender.
